name: A King's Tribute
summary: Magni Bronzebeard honors Sully Balloo with a memorial in Ironforge. Granite from Lordaeron gives the fallen dwarf a lasting place in his people's memory.

sections.title: A Monument Carved in Grief
sections.body: King Magni Bronzebeard ordered a monument for Sully Balloo, a dwarf who died serving his people. Grand Mason Marblesten carved it from fine granite brought from Lordaeron's war-torn lands. The memorial now stands in Ironforge, honoring soldiers whose sacrifices help preserve the dwarven kingdom.

sections.title: A Sovereign's Reflection
sections.body: When told the monument is complete, Magni reflects on stone and mortality. Carved rock can never equal a brave dwarf's life, he knows, but he hopes the memorial endures. Generations walking Azeroth may then remember the heroes who bled to secure their tomorrow.

faq.q: Who is being honored by this memorial?
faq.answer: The memorial honors Sully Balloo, a brave dwarven soldier who gave his life fighting for his people and the Alliance.

faq.q: Why was the stone gathered from Lordaeron?
faq.answer: Grand Mason Marblesten needed fine granite for a lasting royal tribute. Lordaeron is known for exceptional quarried stone, though the region lies in ruin after the Scourge.

faq.q: Where does this quest take place?
faq.answer: You meet Grand Mason Marblesten, then bring word to King Magni Bronzebeard in Ironforge's High Seat.

faq.q: Why does King Magni commission this tribute personally?
faq.answer: Magni believes rulers must honor the foot soldiers who defend their realms. He wants the memorial to remind future generations of the price common soldiers paid for their safety.

faq.q: What happens after the memorial is finished?
faq.answer: Reporting to King Magni completes the memorial chain. The statue remains in Ironforge as a permanent landmark honoring Sully Balloo.

faq.q: What is the masonry significance of the statue?
faq.answer: Grand Mason Marblesten is among Ironforge's most accomplished dwarven artisans. He shaped imported Lordaeron granite into a fitting national work of art for the monarch.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you share a tradition of honoring fallen ancestral warriors in enduring stone.
The monument reminds you of the heavy toll recent conflicts exacted across Khaz Modan and the northern kingdoms.
As a warrior, you hear Magni honor the selfless valor of frontline soldiers like Sully Balloo, who gave everything in battle.
